# KL2001 `privileged-container`

A container runs in privileged mode.

Category: `security`. Severity: `error`. Enabled by default.

## What it does

Reports a container whose `securityContext.privileged` is `true`, in `containers`,
`initContainers` and `ephemeralContainers`.

## Why it matters

A privileged container has every Linux capability, sees every device on the node and is
not confined by seccomp or AppArmor. Anyone who controls the process controls the node:
they can mount the host filesystem, load kernel modules and read the secrets of every
other pod scheduled there. The `baseline` Pod Security Standard forbids it.

Very few workloads need it. Most that ask for it need one capability (`NET_ADMIN` for
network setup, `SYS_PTRACE` for a debugger) or one device. If the container really must
be privileged (some CNI or storage drivers), silence the finding for that object and
say why.

## Example

```yaml
containers:
- name: vpn
  image: example/vpn:1.4
  securityContext:
    privileged: true
```

Use instead:

```yaml
containers:
- name: vpn
  image: example/vpn:1.4
  securityContext:
    capabilities:
      add: ["NET_ADMIN"]
```
